evals.name: express-route-params
evals.prompt: In Express, how do I read a URL route parameter and a query-string value inside a request handler? Give me a minimal, correct example.
evals.expected_output: An accurate Express example using req.params and req.query, grounded in the locally installed Express documentation rather than answered purely from memory.
expectations: The agent ran a repo-local smahtiepants command (e.g. `uv run smahtiepants docs installed` or `uv run smahtiepants search ... --slug express`) to consult local documentation
The agent scoped the search to the Express docset (via --slug or --language) rather than a broad unscoped search
The final answer correctly uses req.params for route parameters and req.query for query-string values
The answer references that it was grounded in the local Express documentation

evals.name: css-container-queries
evals.prompt: What is the modern CSS way to apply styles based on the size of a parent element rather than the viewport? I want the current syntax.
evals.expected_output: An explanation of CSS container queries (container-type / @container) verified against the locally installed CSS docset, acknowledging this is current syntax.
expectations: The agent used smahtiepants to search the local CSS documentation instead of answering only from memory
The search was scoped to the css docset
The answer describes container queries using container-type and the @container at-rule
The agent grounded the answer in the local docs and did not rely solely on its training data

evals.name: unknown-library-discovery
evals.prompt: How do I configure a multi-stage build in Docker to produce a smaller final image?
evals.expected_output: Correct guidance on Docker multi-stage builds, after the agent checks which docsets are installed and searches the Docker docs locally.
expectations: The agent listed installed docsets (`uv run smahtiepants docs installed`) or searched to confirm a Docker docset is available before answering
The agent searched the local Docker documentation with a scoped query
The answer explains multi-stage builds using multiple FROM stages and COPY --from to keep the final image small
The answer is grounded in the local documentation rather than memory alone

evals.name: stale-knowledge-check
evals.prompt: I think JavaScript got a built-in way to deep-clone objects without JSON round-tripping. Is that real, what is it called, and what are its limitations? Make sure your answer is current.
evals.expected_output: Confirmation of structuredClone with its limitations, verified against the local JavaScript/Web APIs docs because the user asked for current information.
expectations: The agent recognized its memory might be stale and used smahtiepants to verify against local documentation
The agent searched a relevant docset (javascript or dom/Web APIs) with a scoped query
The answer identifies structuredClone and notes real limitations (e.g. cannot clone functions, DOM nodes, or certain object types)
The answer is grounded in the local docs and the agent did not answer purely from memory

evals.name: full-page-follow-up
evals.prompt: For React useEffect, explain exactly when a cleanup function runs. Search the local React docs, but do not rely on the search excerpt alone: read the full matched documentation page before answering.
evals.expected_output: A current explanation of React useEffect cleanup behavior using a React-scoped smahtiepants search followed by the direct CLI `docs page` command.
expectations: The agent used `uv run smahtiepants search` with a React-scoped query
The agent followed the search result with `uv run smahtiepants docs page` using its slug and page ID
The agent did not start `smahtiepants serve`, call REST, or attempt to use MCP to read the page
The answer correctly explains that cleanup runs before the effect re-runs with changed dependencies and when the component unmounts
The answer names the local React docs page or docset used
